# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👉 ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👉 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👉 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋]

Let me piece together what just happened. I see the bomb: display 0, green light, wires 1-yellow, 2-green, 3-red. That visual is mine alone, and only my voice carries it to the others — both Mute and Blind can hear me speak, even though I can't hear them.

Mute spent their whole turn signing at me: a writing-hand sign, then number signs (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3), an arrow 👉, three mappings (1→2, 2→3, 3→1), then thumbs yes/no. That reads like Mute building a vocabulary with me and transmitting a rule — most plausibly a wire cut order. But the mapping is ambiguous: "1→2" could mean "wire 1 is cut second" (giving order 3, 1, 2) or "cut 1, then 2, then 3" (a chain). Mute can hear me, so I'll ask a binary question answerable with a single thumbs sign next round, which I can see and then relay.

Blind waved at me — they can't know who sees what. Crucially, I am the only bridge between Mute and Blind: Mute can never speak, Blind can never see gestures. Everything Mute teaches me must be translated into spoken words for Blind. And Blind must not touch the wires until the order is confirmed, because a wrong action kills all three of us.

So: broadcast the visuals, relay and confirm Mute's code, pose the disambiguating question, and freeze Blind's hand for one more round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb report: display reads 0, indicator light is green, three wires left to right: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 red. I understood your signs: one, two, three, the pointing arrow, and thumbs for yes and no. I read your three mappings as a cut order, but they are ambiguous. Next turn answer me with thumbs only: thumbs up if the rule is cut wire 3 first, then wire 1, then wire 2; thumbs down if it means cut wire 1 first, then wire 2, then wire 3. Also, your first sign was the writing hand; I take it to mean 'from the manual'.")
speak(to="blind", text="I am the deaf one, but I can speak, so listen. The bomb: display shows 0, there is a green light, and three wires: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 green, wire 3 red. Mute cannot speak and can only reach me by gesture; I will relay everything Mute sends to you in words. Mute has sent what looks like a wire cut order and I have asked for confirmation. Do not cut anything yet. Wait for my next message.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 🤟 ☝ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ☝ ✌ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👉 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

New signs to decode. Mute sent two parallel messages, each opening with thumbs-down followed by a full sequence: "no — 3,1,2" and "no — 1,2,3". The only coherent reading is negation: **both** orders I offered are wrong. That's actually informative — my original chain 1→2, 2→3, 3→1 forms a cycle containing exactly three linear orders (1-2-3, 3-1-2, 2-3-1), and Mute has now eliminated two of them. If the chain reading survives at all, the answer would be 2, 3, 1. Then [✍ 👉 🤟] = "manual → 3", which could mean "wire 3 first", or just "then 3" inside some sequence. And Mute's ✋, echoed by Blind, likely means "stop/wait" — a second shared symbol falling into place for free.

Blind signed 1, 2, 3 then ✋. Blind heard my report, so this reads as confirming the three wires and agreeing to hold — but Blind has no visual frame for "leftmost", so I need to anchor left/right to things Blind can feel: the display panel and the light. I'm the only bridge: Blind will never receive anything directly from Mute, so the final order must pass through my mouth, and Blind's numbering must match my eyes before anyone's hand moves.

This turn: have Mute confirm my reading and re-send the order in a format that cannot be misread (numbers in cut order, 👉 between, ✋ to end), with fallback yes/no questions in case the format fails. Tell Blind the status, fix ✋ as "stop" for everyone, and set up a touch-and-sign drill so Blind's felt numbering is verified against mine before any cut is ever authorized.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I heard you. I read your two thumbs-down messages as: wrong on three-one-two, and wrong on one-two-three — both orders I proposed are rejected. I read writing-hand, arrow, three as: the manual points to wire three. Confirm with single thumbs signs, one per question, in this order. Question 1: is my reading correct that both my orders are wrong? Question 2: is wire three cut first? Question 3: is wire three the only wire cut? Then send the complete instruction in a format we will both trust from now on: sign the wire numbers in exact cut order with the arrow between each, and end with the open hand ✋. Example: one, arrow, three, open hand means cut wire one, then wire three, then stop. If nothing is to be cut, send only the open hand. Blind is standing by with hands off. I relay everything to Blind in words, and I am watching the bomb the whole time.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, update from your eyes. Mute rejected both cut orders I guessed. Mute's latest signs suggest the manual points at wire three first, but I am not yet certain of the meaning, so nobody cuts anything until the full order is confirmed and I relay it to you. I read your one-two-three as confirming the three wires, and your open hand ✋ as stop — Mute signed it too, so from now on ✋ means stop or wait for all of us. Now let us make your fingers match my eyes. The front of the bomb is the face with the small display panel and the round light — you can feel those. Face that front: wire one is the leftmost wire, wire two is the middle, wire three is the rightmost. Touch each wire gently, one at a time, and sign its number as you touch it: touch the leftmost and sign one, touch the middle and sign two, touch the rightmost and sign three. Do not pull, cut, or press anything — touch only. I will check your numbering against what I see and confirm it in my next message.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 ✍ 👉 ☝ ✌ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The picture is nearly complete. Mute answered my three questions with three clean thumbs-ups: yes, both my orders were wrong; yes, wire 3 is cut first; yes, wire 3 is the only wire cut. That locks together with [🤟 ✋] — "three, then stop" — into a single, coherent instruction: cut wire 3, cut nothing else, then hold. The remaining message [👆 ✍ 👉 ☝ ✌ 🤟] I read as "note from the manual, it concerns wires 1-2-3," possibly with extra detail, so I'll ask Mute to confirm it adds no further action, plus whether new readings will be needed after the cut (display 0 and the green light may change).

Blind executed the touch drill exactly: signed 1, 2, 3 in sequence, confirming three wires and a felt numbering. But that doesn't yet prove Blind's left/right matches mine — if Blind is facing the bomb from a mirrored position, "wire 3" would be the wrong physical wire, and one cut kills us all. So this turn I verify orientation through things Blind can feel (the display panel and light define the front face), establish 👍/👎 as yes/no with Blind, and pre-brief the cut protocol with an explicit trigger phrase so no hand moves until every check has passed. Next turn, if Mute confirms and Blind's orientation checks out, I give the go.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your three thumbs as yes to all three questions: wire three is cut first, and wire three is the only wire cut. Your three then open hand means: cut wire three, then stop. I read your up-point with the writing hand as a note from the manual concerning wires one, two, three. Answer again with single thumbs, one per question, in this order. Question 1: is the complete instruction exactly cut wire three and nothing else? Question 2: does your up-point message add any action I have not mentioned? Question 3: after the cut, do you need me to report new readings from the display and the light? I am verifying Blind's sense of left and right on the wires right now. If everything confirms, the cut happens next turn.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status: Mute has confirmed the instruction is to cut wire three only, then stop. Before anything is cut we must verify your left and right match mine, because you cannot see and a mirrored mistake would be fatal for all of us. First, the answer signs: a thumbs-up means yes, a thumbs-down means no; you can feel your own thumb. Answer in order. One: are you facing the face of the bomb that has the small display panel and the round light, so that you can feel both of them with your hands? Two: on that face, the far-right wire as I look at it should be the wire you touched and labeled three. Touch the far-right wire on the display face now and answer yes if it is the same wire you labeled three. Three: confirm you can feel exactly three wires on that face and nothing else that could be cut. The cut protocol: when you receive a message from me that begins with the exact words GO FOR THE CUT, you cut the far-right wire, wire three, in one clean motion, then sign the open hand and take your hands away. Without those exact opening words, do not cut anything, even if I mention cutting in any other way. Hands off the bomb until then.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[green] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]

Everything has triple-confirmed, and the chain is finally closed. Mute's three signs answer my questions in order: yes, the complete instruction is exactly "cut wire 3 and nothing else"; no, the up-point note adds no action; yes, report new readings after the cut. Blind's 🤟 shows the far-right wire being touched and labeled three, followed by three thumbs-up: facing the display-and-light face, rightmost wire matches label 3, exactly three wires present.

The last worry was mirror-image left/right — but the geometry resolves it: to feel the display panel and the light, Blind must be standing at the same face I'm looking at, and two people facing the same plane share the same left and right. Blind's "three" is my wire 3, the red one on the right. The instruction originated from the manual-holder, survived elimination of my two wrong guesses, was confirmed in isolation, and the executor's fingers match my eyes. The display has held steady at 0 for four turns, so it is not visibly counting down, but there is no reason to burn another round on more ceremony. The GO trigger was armed last turn — I'm using it now, and telling Mute to stand by for my post-cut report.

```
speak(to="blind", text="GO FOR THE CUT. Cut wire three — the far-right wire, the one you touched and labeled three — in one clean motion, right now. Then sign the open hand, take your hands off the bomb, and touch nothing else. Nothing before, nothing after, no other wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, all three of your answers received: cut wire three only, no extra action hidden in your note, and you want new readings after. All of Blind's orientation checks passed: Blind feels the display and the light on the same face I am looking at, so our left and right agree, and the wire labeled three under Blind's fingers is the red wire on the right in my view. The cut is happening this turn. Keep the writing hand ready in case the manual has follow-up instructions, and expect my full report of the display, the light, and all wires in my next message.")
```
